newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Oct gas oil traded at $27.85, up $1.25.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Oct gas oil traded at $27.85, up $1.25.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps went on rising as bids kept going up and offers remained scarce on Tuesday after the United States said it had fired cruise missiles at targets in Iraq, industry sources said.
October gas oil swaps, the most actively traded product in Singapore, were traded at $27.85 per barrel with more buyers seen looking for firm offers, brokers said.
The deal at $27.85 per barrel was up about $1.25 per barrel from Monday's close. Earlier on Tuesday, October swaps were traded at $27.30 and $27.50 per barrel.
Brokers said offers were notionally at around $28.00 per barrel for October swaps with no firm sellers seen for September.
September swaps bid was at $27.90 per barrel with no firm offers seen, brokers said.
Jet fuel fuel prices also soared, with September bids seen at $31.00 per barrel over Friday's trades at $29.50 per barrel, one broker said.
Brokers said there was some panic buying as a few players who were caught short decided to cover their positions.
Liquidity remained thin for the other oil products. Bids for September fuel oil were at $111.50 per tonne, up $2.00 per tonne from Monday's close, and not finding firm offers, brokers said.
